title: The Nativity of Mary (8 September)
hookLine: nine months after the Immaculate Conception, a birthday for Mary
tomorrow: The Exaltation of the Cross (14 September)

cards: Count back nine months from the eighth of September, and you land on the eighth of December: the Immaculate Conception, the feast of Mary's conception in her mother's womb.
The Church's calendar does the arithmetic on purpose. So today is a birthday. In Malta it's a public holiday; in Italian towns and in parts of India there are processions and sweets.
And the Gospel the Church reads for it is one that's easy to skip: the long list of names at the start of Matthew.

teach.h: NOT IN THE BIBLE; A TRADITION.
teach.b: Like her parents' names, Mary's birth isn't told in the Bible.
The details again come from the Protoevangelium of James, and an old tradition places her birth in Jerusalem, near the pool of Bethesda, where a church of Saint Anne stands today.
The feast began in the East, and Rome took it up later. So why read a genealogy on her birthday?

Matthew counts it out as three sets of fourteen generations, from Abraham through David and the exile, and it's not all heroes: a man who helped sell his brother, a king who arranged a soldier's death, and women with complicated stories, Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Urias.
Ordinary, mixed-up people, generation after generation.

Then the list breaks its own pattern. Line after line, it's been so-and-so begot so-and-so. At the end, in the Douay-Rheims: "And Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
The rhythm stops at her. Mary's birthday is the Church saying: here is where the long, crooked family line was heading.

teach.h: OF WHOM WAS BORN JESUS, WHO IS CALLED CHRIST.
teach.b: One ordinary-looking girl, born, tradition says, to an older couple, in a city full of pilgrims.

Catholics greet her today, often with the angel's own words from Luke: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women." There's no cake in the liturgy. But in some towns, there is cake.

how: Catholics keep the feast of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary on 8 September, nine months after the Immaculate Conception; the Gospel is Matthew's genealogy, and in places such as Malta and parts of Italy and India the day is marked with processions and festivals.

games.q: you're choosing the Gospel for Mary's birthday Mass. the Bible has no story of her birth. what does the Church choose?
games.why: the genealogy: generation after generation of mixed-up people, and the rhythm stops at Mary, of whom was born Jesus.

practice: Think about the people in the line that led to you: names you know, names you don't.
If you pray, greet Mary the way Catholics do, Hail, full of grace, and wish her a happy birthday; it's a simple, almost childlike thing, and that's the point.
If you don't pray, think of a birthday you've forgotten lately, and how you might honor it.

wordCard.voice: Nativitas Mariae. Latin for the birth of Mary, kept nine months after the Immaculate Conception, on the eighth of September. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the birth of Mary, the feast's name.
